i think it’s further out, likely closer to middle or end of next year 

a. limitations of current consumer hardware

i would use ai more but typing & waiting takes too much time and it’s rarely the time/place to use voice. 

ar glasses, brain input, or a device that lets you mouth the words but not have to say them out loud, and ofcs super low latency 

b. entertainment/slop

only way token usage explodes in the exponential is the rise of ai strictly for non-productive uses. personalized content or replacement to doomscrolling 

typing & reading long essay responses stimulate a different part of ur brain than watching tiktoks or netflix. humans clearly gravitate to the latter en masse.

c. data/ip

imo llm’s are useless to 90% of population without personal data

licensing deals, security, and portability of your personal data will be a massive hurdle to overcome for agents to become integral part of everyone’s daily lives

lots of struggle ahead for this as many tech companies entire moats are their user data and many consumer biz entire moats are their IP

so however payouts and interconnectivity are solved will either make everything silo’d or lead to explosion of new biz creation similar to dropshipping

—

until we start crossing these chasms, for the most part all potential best case scenarios for ai coding (curing cancer, automating white collar work, etc) is mostly priced in
